questions.question: What does saving mean in personal finance?
choices: Borrowing to increase present consumption
Spending income before receiving it
Setting aside money rather than spending it now
Selling an asset at any price

questions.question: What is an emergency fund intended to cover?
choices: Unexpected necessary expenses or interruptions in income
Only planned vacation expenses
Regular purchases of speculative assets
Only expenses already paid by insurance

questions.question: What does liquidity describe?
choices: The maximum possible return of an investment
The number of depositors at a bank
The length of a person's employment history
How easily an asset can be accessed or converted to cash

questions.question: What is compound interest?
choices: Interest paid only on the original deposit
Interest earned on principal and previously earned interest
A fee paid for every cash withdrawal
A tax charged only on household spending

questions.question: What is a savings goal?
choices: A planned purpose and target amount for money set aside
The maximum borrowing limit on a credit card
A guarantee that prices will stay unchanged
A lender's plan to collect overdue payments

questions.question: What does APY help a saver compare?
choices: The number of branches a bank operates
The risk of every stock in a portfolio
Annual deposit earnings including the effect of compounding
The amount of sales tax on a purchase

questions.question: What is an automatic savings transfer?
choices: A loan automatically charged to a credit card
A tax refund issued after every purchase
A promise of a guaranteed stock return
A scheduled movement of money into a savings account

questions.question: Why can a specific deadline improve a savings plan?
choices: It removes every possible unexpected expense
It helps determine how much must be saved each period
It guarantees that income will rise before the deadline
It makes account fees irrelevant to the goal

questions.question: Why is access to funds important when planning emergency savings?
choices: Emergencies may require money before a long-term asset can be sold
Emergency funds are useful only after retirement
All unexpected expenses arrive on a predictable schedule
Liquidity guarantees the highest investment return

questions.question: How can inflation affect money saved over time?
choices: It increases the number of dollars in every account automatically
It prevents banks from paying any interest
It can reduce what the saved dollars can purchase
It turns every savings account into a loan

questions.question: Why might a saver compare account fees before choosing an account?
choices: Fees always raise the account's interest rate
Fees are unrelated to the balance remaining
Fees guarantee that a bank has more deposit insurance
Fees can reduce the benefit of interest earnings

questions.question: What tradeoff may come with a certificate of deposit compared with an ordinary savings account?
choices: A CD must always allow unlimited withdrawals without penalties
A CD may offer a fixed rate but restrict early access
A CD represents ownership shares in a business
A CD automatically adjusts to every increase in prices

questions.question: Why can beginning to save earlier help with a long-term goal?
choices: It provides more time for contributions and potential compounding
It guarantees that every saver earns the same interest rate
It eliminates the need to check account conditions
It makes future contributions unnecessary in every case

questions.question: What does paying yourself first mean as a savings habit?
choices: Skipping required loan payments to buy optional goods
Waiting until all discretionary spending is finished
Setting aside planned savings when income arrives
Withdrawing savings whenever income increases

questions.question: Why might separate savings categories help a household?
choices: They guarantee each account earns a higher rate
They eliminate the need to track balances
They automatically double the household's total savings
They make progress toward different goals easier to track

questions.question: A student needs $600 in six months and already has $120. Ignoring interest, how much must be saved monthly?
An account earns 5% simple interest on $200 for one year, with no fees. How much interest does it earn?
A $100 deposit earns 10% interest annually, compounded once a year. With no transactions or fees, what is the balance after two years?
An account earns $12 in interest but charges $18 in fees over the same year. What is the net change from these two items?
choices: A $30 increase
A $6 increase
An $18 decrease
A $6 decrease

questions.question: A person's goal is a necessary purchase next month. Which feature should receive particular attention when choosing where to hold the money?
choices: Potential returns over several decades
Reliable short-term access and preservation of the funds
The popularity of an unrelated company's stock
The chance of a large gain from a volatile asset
